article_content: Crunchyroll, a prominent anime streaming platform, has recently been in the news. Although the initial announcement was misleading, it wasn't about resolving the issues with its smart TV app. Rather, the company introduced a new FAST channel and reached a settlement in a class-action lawsuit. As a Sony subsidiary, Crunchyroll is a primary destination for legally streaming anime in the US at an affordable price. It provides same-day broadcasts of Japanese shows, including both dubbed and subtitled versions, and features a vast collection of notable anime series from the last two decades. Nevertheless, the service functions optimally on mobile devices and web browsers, whereas the smart TV app is marred by frequent crashes and technical glitches.
